topic: The 1859 Carrington storm and the 2012 near miss: a 30-second sample
method: Claims C1-C6 read on NASA Science's article (full page, 2026-11-12) and the Commons file record. The Lloyd's 2013 cost estimate was left out because its report did not open.

claims.claim: In September 1859 the English astronomer Richard Carrington saw a solar flare with his own eyes while drawing a sunspot group; his drawing of the sunspots is dated 1 September 1859, and the letters A-D mark where the white light appeared.

sources.title: NASA Science: Near Miss: The Solar Superstorm of July 2012 (22 Jul 2014)
sources.quote: [read 2026-11-12] Carrington ... actually saw the instigating flare with his own eyes

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons: Carrington Richard drawing of 1859 sunspots (file metadata: date 1859-09-01, public domain)
sources.quote: [read 2026-11-12] Drawing of sunspots by Richard Carrington ... Date 1 September 1859

sources.title: Carrington, R. C. (1859) Description of a Singular Appearance seen in the Sun on September 1, 1859. MNRAS 20, 13
sources.quote: [record confirmed via Crossref 2026-11-12: MNRAS, 11 Nov 1859] the original paper

claims.notes: What A-D mark comes from Carrington's paper as summarised by secondary sources; the narration only says the sunspots flashed white.

claims.claim: In the days after Carrington's observation, powerful CMEs hit Earth, and Northern Lights were seen as far south as Cuba.

sources.title: NASA Science: Near Miss: The Solar Superstorm of July 2012 (22 Jul 2014)
sources.quote: [read 2026-11-12] ignited Northern Lights as far south as Cuba

claims.notes: Reported on NASA's account. The primary 1859-60 accounts (Loomis, 'The great auroral exhibition of August 28th to September 4th, 1859', American Journal of Science, 1860, doi:10.2475/ajs.s2-29.85.92 and later parts) were found but not read: read them before calling this verified.

claims.claim: The 1859 storm caused telegraph lines around the world to spark, setting fire to some telegraph offices.

sources.title: NASA Science: Near Miss: The Solar Superstorm of July 2012 (22 Jul 2014)
sources.quote: [read 2026-11-12] caused global telegraph lines to spark, setting fire to some telegraph offices

claims.notes: How many offices burned is not documented; the narration says 'some'. Reported on NASA's account. The primary 1859-60 accounts (Loomis, 'The great auroral exhibition of August 28th to September 4th, 1859', American Journal of Science, 1860, doi:10.2475/ajs.s2-29.85.92 and later parts) were found but not read: read them before calling this verified.

claims.claim: On 23 July 2012 an extreme solar storm, comparable to Carrington's, crossed Earth's orbit and missed; had it erupted one week earlier, Earth would have been in the line of fire (Daniel Baker, University of Colorado).

sources.title: NASA Science: Near Miss: The Solar Superstorm of July 2012 (22 Jul 2014)
sources.quote: [read 2026-11-12] If the eruption had occurred only one week earlier, Earth would have been in the line of fire

sources.title: Baker, D. N. et al. (2013) A major solar eruptive event in July 2012: Defining extreme space weather scenarios. Space Weather 11
sources.quote: [record confirmed via Crossref 2026-11-12] the study NASA reports, by the scientist quoted

claims.notes: Other outlets say the CME left the Sun on 22 July; the orbit crossing is 23 July.

claims.claim: Pete Riley (2012) calculated a 12% chance that a Carrington-class storm would hit Earth in the following ten years.

sources.title: NASA Science: Near Miss: The Solar Superstorm of July 2012 (22 Jul 2014)
sources.quote: [read 2026-11-12] he calculated the odds that a Carrington-class storm would hit Earth in the next ten years. The answer: 12%

claims.notes: A 2012 statistical estimate for 2012-2022, shown with an ESTIMATE badge and the study year.

claims.claim: Analysts believe a direct hit by an extreme CME like July 2012's could cause widespread blackouts, disabling everything that plugs into a wall socket.

sources.title: NASA Science: Near Miss: The Solar Superstorm of July 2012 (22 Jul 2014)
sources.quote: [read 2026-11-12] could cause widespread power blackouts, disabling everything that plugs into a wall socket
